correctness.rationale: The frozen quantifier over any real or complex Hilbert space is false: for H={0}, e.g. K_{3,1} has the inequality for all inputs, and all part sizes have best nonnegative constant 0. The complete replacements in repairs/2 restrict to nonzero H and explicitly describe {0}; this closes the gap without changing any graph size or scalar result. Recheck: the Laplacian decomposes the centered input into two supported contrasts of eigenvalues n and m and the block-constant mode of eigenvalue m+n. Integration gives the normalized off-diagonal coefficient 4 lambda mu/(lambda+mu)^2, strictly in (0,1) for either contrast versus the block mode. On each part let X=||u_i||^2+||a||^2, beta_i=Re<u_i,a>. The pointwise fourth-power difference is 4(1-rho)X beta_i+4(1-rho^2)beta_i^2. The constant ||a||^2 contribution cancels in the sum; on parts of size two the opposite contrasts have equal norms so the remaining cubic term cancels, and on singleton parts there is no contrast. The squared terms give the exact equality characterization. The nonzero between-part mode along a unit vector proves sharpness even at K_{1,1}. On a size-at-least-three part the contrast (2,-1,-1,0,...) has both sum of cubes and sum of squares equal to 6. With block value -1/4 and opposite mean chosen to center the total, the deficit is -(3/2)(1-rho)(3-rho)<0, with no contrast on the other part. Relabeling and embedding along a unit vector handles all sizes and fields.
